results.notes: NostrWebsocketClient.Streams.EventStream/EoseStream (Rx) after client.Send(new NostrRequest(sub, filter)). The client does not verify: per event the harness calls the library's NostrEvent.ComputeId() (re-serializes the event with Newtonsoft.Json) and compares it with Id, then NostrEvent.IsSignatureValid() (BIP-340 over Id). Websocket.Client reconnection and its no-message reconnect timeout are turned off.

ConnectAndWaitUntilConnected (polls the socket state every 100 ms) is untimed. The client verifies every event before raising it: NostrExtensions.Verify() recomputes the id (its own string-built NIP-01 serialization, SHA-256) and checks the BIP-340 signature; failing events are dropped. Frames go through an unbounded Channel to one processing task (System.Text.Json JsonDocument + Deserialize<NostrEvent>).

The enumeration ends at the EOSE; the end of the await foreach is the EOSE time. results.api: RelayClient.ConnectAsync + client.SubscribeAsync (IAsyncEnumerable<SubscriptionEvent>), single relay, no pool
results.notes: RelayClient verifies every event (NostrEvent.Verify: recomputed id + BIP-340) before it reaches a subscription and drops failures silently; frames are parsed with System.Text.Json JsonDocument. The top-level NostrClient.SubscribeAsync hides the EOSE, so the harness uses the layer below it, which yields it.

RelayClient verifies every event (NostrEvent.Verify: recomputed id + BIP-340) before it reaches a subscription and drops failures silently; frames are parsed with System.Text.Json JsonDocument. The top-level NostrClient.SubscribeAsync hides the EOSE, so the harness uses the layer below it, which yields it. A pool (multi-relay layer) with one relay: a variant. Auto-reconnect/resubscribe are its defaults (no reconnect happens).

results.crypto: libsecp256k1 (C, via rust secp256k1 0.30 / secp256k1-sys 0.10, in libnostr_sdk_ffi.so)
results.notes: Rust library (nostr-sdk 0.45.2, nostr 0.45.3, serde_json) behind UniFFI: every event crosses the FFI (a Next() async call per event, the Event object is a handle; its id is read with event.Id().ToHex()). The relay pool verifies id and signature of every event before delivering it and drops NIP-40-expired events. The stream ends at EOSE (ExitOnEose); its end is the EOSE time. StreamEvents runs through rust-nostr's fixed internal channels (the relay's notification broadcast, then the stream's own channel), whose sizes the bindings do not expose. Client.AddRelay(url, RelayCapabilities.Read(), ...) (the C# binding takes the capabilities explicitly; the Rust default is read + write, and ReqTarget.Auto sends the REQ to read relays either way) + Connect are untimed. alloc_bytes counts only the managed side (handles, strings); the Rust heap is not counted.

Blockcore's fork of Nostr.Client (adds NIP-44/PoW; same receive path). NostrWebsocketClient.Streams.EventStream/EoseStream (Rx) after client.Send(new NostrRequest(sub, filter)). The client does not verify: per event the harness calls the library's NostrEvent.ComputeId() (re-serializes the event with Newtonsoft.Json) and compares it with Id, then NostrEvent.IsSignatureValid() (BIP-340 over Id). Websocket.Client reconnection and its no-message reconnect timeout are turned off.

F# library used from C#. Its receive loop verifies every EVENT (Event.verify: recomputed id + BIP-340) and hands the callback a Result: Ok(RMEvent) for valid events, Error for invalid or undecodable ones (counted as rejected). JSON via Thoth.Json.Net 12.0.0 (Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.1 underneath). License file: GPL-2.0.

results.api: NSRelay.TryConnect + OnEvent/OnEose events + SendFilter(NRequestReq), one relay
results.notes: Last release 2023. NSRelay does not verify, and NEvent.IsVerified() checks BIP-340 over the id it recomputes (GetId) without ever comparing it with the event's Id. So per event the harness calls the library's own id function (the private NEvent.GetId, Newtonsoft.Json + SHA-256, by reflection) once, compares it with Id, then checks the signature over Id with NPub.FromHex(PubKey).IsHexSignatureValid(Sig, Id), the call IsVerified makes. NSRelay queues frames and its dispatch loop sleeps 200 ms whenever the queue is empty; it splits every frame on ',' to find the message type. GetId serializes a temporary NEventSign that shares the event's Tags list and disposes it, which clears that list: the first id is right, but the event is left without tags and any later GetId (or IsVerified) hashes an empty tag list, hence one id computation per event. NTag holds a key and at most 4 values, so a valid event with a longer tag (zap-request relays tags, ...) gets a wrong id and is rejected. SendFilter replaces the REQ's subscription id with the relay object's own SubscriptionId (a Guid). TryConnect also fetches NIP-11 over HTTP (untimed).
